name: Meshech
title: Son of Japheth and ancestor of a people
summary: Meshech was a son of Japheth, who was the son of Noah. He is regarded as the ancestor of a people often associated in biblical tradition with regions in Asia Minor (Anatolia). Meshech is mentioned several times in the Old Testament, particularly in prophetic texts in Ezekiel, where his people are mentioned together with Tubal and Gog from the land of Magog.

keyEvents.title: Meshech's birth and genealogy
keyEvents.description: Meshech is mentioned as one of the sons of Japheth in the table of nations after the flood. He is part of Noah's descendants who spread across the earth.

keyEvents.title: Repetition in the Books of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Meshek is listed again among the sons of Japheth in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles, confirming his place in the history of nations.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Book of Psalms
keyEvents.description: The psalmist laments living among the people of Meshek, symbolizing foreign and hostile nations far from God's people.

keyEvents.title: Prophecy against Gog from the land of Magog
keyEvents.description: Ezekiel prophesies against Gog, prince of Rosh, Meshek, and Tubal, predicting God's judgment upon them in the last days.

keyEvents.title: Lament over Meshek and Tubal
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's lament over fallen nations, Meshek and Tubal are mentioned among the mighty nations that have perished and lie in the realm of the dead.

keyEvents.title: Meshek in Ezekiel's prophecy against Tyre regarding trade
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's prophecy against Tyre, Meshek and Tubal are mentioned as trading partners who dealt in slaves and bronze utensils.
